definitions.explanation: The tabular arrangement of chemical elements organized by atomic number, showing periodic trends in their properties.

examples.japanese: {周期表|しゅうきひょう}を{覚|おぼ}えた。
{周期表|しゅうきひょう}で{元素|げんそ}の{位置|いち}を{確認|かくにん}した。
examples.english: I checked the element's position on the periodic table.

examples.japanese: {化学|かがく}の{授業|じゅぎょう}で{周期表|しゅうきひょう}の{見方|みかた}を{習|なら}い、{元素|げんそ}の{性質|せいしつ}の{規則性|きそくせい}を{学|まな}んだ。
examples.english: In chemistry class, we learned how to read the periodic table and studied the patterns in element properties.

notes:
The standard term for the periodic table of elements. Composed of {周期|しゅうき} (period, cycle) + {表|ひょう} (table, chart). A fundamental concept in chemistry education.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {周期表|しゅうきひょう}の{元素|げんそ}: elements on the periodic table
- {周期表|しゅうきひょう}を{暗記|あんき}する: to memorize the periodic table
- {周期表|しゅうきひょう}の{族|ぞく}: groups on the periodic table
- {周期表|しゅうきひょう}の{周期|しゅうき}: periods on the periodic table

RELATED WORDS:
- {元素|げんそ}: element
- {原子番号|げんしばんごう}: atomic number
- {化学記号|かがくきごう}: chemical symbol
- {周期律|しゅうきりつ}: periodic law

CULTURAL NOTE:
Japanese students commonly memorize the periodic table using mnemonics based on the Japanese readings of element names. The phrase "{水兵|すいへい}リーベ{僕|ぼく}の{船|ふね}" (H, He, Li, Be, B, C, N, O, F, Ne) is one of the most famous.
